 Tesla proposes new $3.1 billion refinery for solar manufacturing in Nueces County
 Andrea Guzmán Thu, November 19, 2026 at 1:54 PM PST TSLA -2.86%

 Learn more Tesla CEO Elon Musk, left, sits with Texas Gov. Greg Abbott at a groundbreaking ceremony for the auto manufacturer's Robstown lithium refining facility on May 10, 2023. The Austin automaker is seeking a tax incentive for a proposed $3.1 billion polysilicon refinery in Nueces County. (Angela Piazza/Corpus Christi Caller-Times via AP) Tesla Inc. is proposing a $3.1 billion polysilicon refinery in Nueces County that would produce raw material for solar cells and other advanced technologies. 
 The project was outlined in an application under Texas' Jobs, Education, Technology and Innovation program, which allows companies to limit the taxable value of eligible property for school district maintenance and operations taxes. The state makes payments to participating school districts to offset some of the tax revenue they otherwise would have received from the property. 
 "While Texas offers significant advantages due to its industrial infrastructure, experienced workforce, strategic Gulf Coast location, and access to energy resources, property tax exposure remains one of the most significant recurring costs associated with the project," Tesla's application says. "As a result, property tax liabilities have a material impact on the project's projected economics and on Tesla's comparison of the Texas location against competing sites under consideration." 
 The Austin-based automaker says the facility would make polysilicon, a key material used in solar cells, helping strengthen the U.S. solar supply chain. The company's application goes on to note that its approval under the incentive program would have "a direct and material influence on Tesla's decision whether to proceed with the project in Texas." 
 Elon Musk's companies have sought such agreements earlier this year for other facilities, warning they could consider other sites if not granted the incentives. 
 Outgoing Gov. Greg Abbott and the rural school districts where Tesla and SpaceX are building a computer chip manufacturing campus signed off on school tax breaks for the so-called Terafab project. And in September, the Lamar Consolidated Independent School District board voted unanimously to approve incentives under the program for a $10 billion solar cell manufacturing facility in suburban Houston. 
 Elon Musk listens as President Donald Trump speaks during an event at the U.S. Institute of Peace on Oct. 8, in Washington. Tesla says a proposed new facility would boost the strength of the domestic solar supply chain. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson) This latest facility proposes a location across several parcels in Robstown, where Tesla already runs a lithium refinery. Of the total $3.1 billion in capital investment that would go toward the polysilicon refinery, $1.5 billion is estimated for engineering and construction, $1.4 billion for equipment and $183 million for development of utility infrastructure. If approved, the incentive period would run from 2031 to 2040. 
 The project would create more than 7,000 one-year jobs during construction, which is expected to run from 2027 through 2030. The project also calls for 515 new employees by 2032 to support operations. Those workers would be paid total compensation that averages $130,000. 
 Story Continues Additionally, an economic analysis prepared for Tesla estimates that the project would support $850 million in total labor income, and nearly $2.5 billion in total economic output across Texas. 
 Philip Carroll, deputy superintendent of Tuloso-Midway Independent School District, where the application has been filed, did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the proposal. 
 Tesla did not offer any further comments. Its application said that the project would "generate substantial economic benefits for the State of Texas," including high-skilled, permanent jobs with wages above the county average, a large temporary construction workforce, new state and local sales and use tax revenue, and a regional ecosystem supporting advanced manufacturing and research activities.
